text:
The city at night transforms into a luminous tapestry, where each skyscraper stands like a solitary pillar of wax, burning with the steady, unyielding flame of electric light. Just as a candle relies on its wick to draw fuel upward and sustain its glow, the urban landscape draws energy from the underground veins of power, channeling it into vertical beacons that pierce the darkness. The skyscrapers are not merely buildings; they are the hardened stearin of the metropolis, solid and structured, yet capable of emitting a warm, inviting radiance that contrasts sharply with the cold, deep indigo of the twilight sky. This sky acts as the vast, unlit room in which these candles dance, their collective brilliance painting an urban masterpiece that wakes up as the rest of the world sleeps, much like a single flame can illuminate an entire room, turning the void into a space of activity and life.

Regarding your priority question: The primary material of a candle is wax.
